pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Music
pageCache.text:
Subject Vision
As a school, we would like to see an increased engagement in Music and performance. We want to expose children further to the joy that music can bring, whilst also giving children an opportunity to use music as a creative outlet within their learning. Linking with the EYFS goals of being ‘Imaginative and Expressive’, we want our children to feel confident to explore music and instruments freely and without the fear of getting it wrong.
In addition, want staff to feel secure in delivering our Music curriculum and to be able to feel the freedom to take children’s inspiration and lead in order to explore and improvise musically. In addition, we want to increase musical knowledge and the children’s understanding of music theory so that written music does not feel completely overwhelming. We have identified a gap within our Music scheme (Charanga) where core musical language is not being explicitly taught. This is a key next step for us when considering our targets within Music, as we want children to be exposed to key Musical literacy. We are also striving to increase participation within Music, especially for those who have SEND needs, and we want to ensure that adaptations are carried out in order to support all children to attend and enjoy Music lessons.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Art
pageCache.text:
Subject Vision
At St Mary’s, our Art and Design curriculum begins in the Early Years through the Creating with Materials and Being Imaginative and Expressive strands of the EYFS Framework, where children are encouraged to explore and experiment with a wide range of media and techniques, developing confidence in expressing their ideas and imagination. This early exploration forms the foundation for a well-sequenced, coherent subject scheme that progressively develops children’s skills and knowledge of visual elements, art forms, artists and art movements as they move through the school. We provide opportunities for pupils to make meaningful links between art and other curriculum areas, deepening understanding and creativity. We want staff to feel secure in delivering a rich and inspiring art curriculum that builds upon the curiosity, imagination and creativity fostered in the Early Years, while also feeling confident to follow children’s ideas and inspiration to explore and improvise where appropriate. Teachers are supported to assess children’s artistic knowledge, skills and creativity accurately and to understand how their year group’s expectations contribute to the wider progression of artistic development across the key stages. Ultimately, we aim for all children to develop a lifelong appreciation of art, increasing their knowledge, confidence and ability to express themselves through a broad and inclusive Art and Design curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Literacy
pageCache.text:
Subject Vision: Writing
At St. Mary’s, we teach children to be reflective and creative writers. Our writing curriculum gives children the tools to write across a range of genres, editing and improving as they go, to produce pieces of work they can be proud of. For every child to play their full part in society, we understand that the teaching of writing is essential for them to gain the knowledge and understanding of how to communicate effectively with the world.
In EYFS and KS1, we focus on establishing strong foundations in the key skills involved in writing, using stories and experiences that bring excitement and creativity to their learning. Children begin by building fine-motor strength, learning letter formation and using their phonic knowledge to spell words through RWI lessons. They then begin to use their developing vocabulary to verbally build sentences, which they will then write using the non-negotiable rules.
In Years 3-6 our writing journeys are based around an engaging core text. Teachers plan exciting writing opportunities across a range of genres and children are clearly shown how to develop their writing skills within these, using a model of excellence to show the children what they’re aiming for and identifying the steps to get there. These steps are adapted to the child and allows every pupil the opportunity to flourish in their writing. Additional grammar and spelling lessons are also taught daily, with extra ‘fluency’ lessons integrated into the writing learning journey to address any gaps. These additional fluency lessons also provide an opportunity to explore the children’s interests outside of the genre or topic being taught. As children progress throughout the school into KS2, we know the importance that editing has on creating a masterpiece. All pupils are encouraged to use these skills to improve their own and others’ writing – recognising and praising their efforts but also looking at how they can improve. We love to celebrate every child’s writing, which is why every final draft is written up beautifully in each child’s ‘Book of Excellence’. This travels with them throughout the school and is a huge celebration of the progress and attainment every child makes in the subject throughout their time at St. Mary’s.
Literacy Long Term Plan 2025-26
Subject Vision: Reading
At St. Mary’s, we believe every child should be able to read for pleasure and develop a life-long love of reading and books. We strive to give children the tools to develop into fluent and enthusiastic readers. It is these tools and opportunities that we believe give our children the necessary skills to become thoughtful and confident readers for life, which helps them to access learning across the entire curriculum and everything they do, in school and beyond.
In EYFS and KS1, children are taught phonics daily, so that they can decode words and begin to develop their fluency and tackle non-familiar words. They also read phonically decodable storybooks, matched to their phonic ability, so that they can begin to develop their comprehension skills. Outside of phonics, we nurture a love of books by exposing the children to a range of engaging and diverse stories to inspire their creativity and capture their imagination. These texts are carefully picked to provide mirrors of characters and settings that reflect themselves, and windows to diverse characters and settings from around the world. There is a strong focus on the teaching of vocabulary during these story explorations, and the texts become familiar to provide a springboard for the EYFS and KS1 writing curriculum. We also have ‘thread texts’ that the children repeatedly engage with from Nursery through to Year 2, that give them a solid foundation in understanding narratives and storytelling – in Nursery and YR these texts are in the reading and play provision and retold orally, in Y1 children learn and retell these stories in a simple written way, and in Y2 the children then innovate these stories and build their creative writing skills in preparation for KS2. In KS2, the reading curriculum builds on fluency and, through their ERIC sessions, provides children with the opportunity to develop and apply their reading and comprehension skills across a variety of texts. Book discussion is also widely encouraged, supporting children to empathise with characters, share opinions and debate topics. We acknowledge and value the important role played by every family in supporting children’s reading development throughout their time at school: this is why we encourage every child in school to read with a family member at least three times per week, communicating their efforts through the home/school reading record and celebrating regular readers, being mindful to support and celebrate those who lack support at home. Reading is at the core of our curriculum here at St. Mary’s, and we truly believe that every child has the ability to read to a high standard as they foster a love of language discovered in books.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Maths
pageCache.text:
Subject Vision
Rooted in our Christian values of Friendship, Kindness, Compassion, and Forgiveness, St Mary’s empowers every child to flourish—just like the lily—growing in confidence, character, and curiosity.
Our carefully designed mathematics curriculum builds strong foundations in number, fluency in key skills, and a resilient, positive attitude towards learning. Children learn to reason, problem-solve, and communicate mathematically with clarity and confidence, developing the skills they need for life.
By fostering a mastery mindset, we ensure that every pupil is supported and challenged to reach their full potential. We nurture independent, reflective learners who understand the purpose and power of mathematics in everyday life and the wider world.
At St Mary’s, we don’t just teach maths—we inspire curious thinkers, lifelong learners, and confident mathematicians.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Physical Education
pageCache.text:
Subject Vision
Physical Education at St Mary’s holds a central role in our whole school curriculum. At St Mary’s Primary School, we aim to encourage the children to be fit and healthy. Pupils are taught the importance of how an active mind creates an active brain, which will then lead to a better mind-set that is focussed and ready for learning. Pupils are given opportunities to try new sports, improve their co-ordination and develop a number of skills which inevitably help with everyday life.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Science
pageCache.text:
Subject Vision
Science at St Mary’s holds a central role in our whole school curriculum. We believe Science is a lens through which children can explore, question and understand the world around them. Our science curriculum sparks pupil curiosity and a desire to understand the science behind their lived experience.
At St Mary’s we endeavour to give pupils the freedom to pose their own questions about the world around them, and we give pupils the agency to decide how best they can investigate answers to their enquiries. They will learn to gather, interpret and present data to draw conclusions, which they will present using appropriate scientific vocabulary.
Throughout their time at St Mary’s pupils will develop a deep understanding of a wide range of scientific topics, helping them to better understand the world around them and their own relationship to it.

What do different phrases/words/letters on my child’s school report mean?
Attainment: The academic standard that pupils reach in, for example, assessments and exams. It’s usually recorded as grades, scores or levels, and it indicates pupils results at the end of a Key Stage.
For Reading, Writing and Maths in KS1 and KS2, pupils working with the curriculum standards will be assigned either Working Towards, Working at, or Greater Depth;those that are working below the curriculum standards will be assessed as Working below.
Attitude to Learning Grading System
At both Key Stages all students will be assessed on their Attitude to Learning across six main areas;

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   EYFS
pageCache.text:
Our Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) provides the very best start to your child’s learning journey. At St Mary’s, we create a warm, stimulating environment where curiosity is celebrated, independence is encouraged, and every child feels valued. We believe that children learn best through play, exploration, and meaningful experiences, supported by caring and skilled staff who extend learning through conversation, questioning, and shared discovery.
Our curriculum is underpinned by the EYFS framework, ensuring that learning is holistic and interconnected across the seven areas of development:
Through a balance of adult-led activities and child-initiated play, we help children develop resilience, confidence, and a love of learning. Our beautiful outdoor spaces provide opportunities for exploration and adventure all year round, supporting physical development and a connection with nature.
We work in close partnership with parents to ensure every child feels happy, secure, and ready to thrive. At St Mary’s, our goal is simple: to give every child the strongest possible foundation for future success.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mary's Primary Academy and Nursery - Folkestone |   Positive Behaviour/Reward System
pageCache.text:
Celebrating Positive Behaviour and Christian Values
At St Mary’s, we believe that recognising positive behaviour plays an important role in building a nurturing, values‑led school community. Our rewards are designed to celebrate pupils who consistently make positive choices, embody our Christian values, and demonstrate exemplary learning behaviours.
Hot Chocolate Champ Award
Each week, teachers nominate children who consistently demonstrate our Christian values of Service, Friendship, Compassion, and Forgiveness, together with excellent learning behaviour.These pupils act as role models within our school, showing sustained commitment to doing the right thing over time.Selected children meet with the Headteacher for our Hot Choc Champ celebration.
This recognition reflects more than a single good week – it celebrates character, kindness, and attitude.
Christian Values Certificate
Every week, one child in each class is awarded the Christian Values Certificate for clearly exemplifying one of our core values in their words, actions, or relationships with others.
The Learner of the Week award recognises exceptional effort or achievement in learning – whether through resilience, perseverance, outstanding work, or personal progress.
We use Class Dojo to recognise the everyday positive choices children make.Pupils can earn Dojo points for:
This mirrors approaches used in many strong primary settings where Dojo points reward effort, behaviour, responsibility and contribution to school life.
Dojo Celebration Assemblies (3 times per year)
Three times a year, we hold a Dojo Assemblyto celebrate pupils’ sustained positive behaviour.During these assemblies, the child in each class who has earned the most Dojo points for that period is recognised and celebrated.
These assemblies help reinforce that recognition is earned through consistency, character, and effort over time — not just one week of good behaviour.
Our Commitment to Fairness and Inclusion
We aim to ensure that all pupils have opportunities to be recognised.Because some children consistently live out our values and behaviours, they may be acknowledged more frequently; however, we regularly reflect on our processes to ensure fairness, balance, and inclusion for all.
Our rewards system is part of our wider behaviour approach, which focuses on:
